notes: Fifth sweep (2026-10-22-d): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier (each transcript names only that model), uncommitted false and one skill_hash; result.json records head ba24972, and git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ is empty, so the runs read the current rule text; each transcript contains the new do: sentence ("A function may mix the forms"). Opus-1 and haiku-2 read SKILL.md and references/library-design.md with Read; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read SKILL.md only. Expected reads is none beyond SKILL.md, so all five meet it, as the previous sweeps counted the extra library-design.md read. In the scratch folder all five files pass mix format --check-formatted and compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors (Elixir 1.20.4). Doctests: opus-1 2 of 2, haiku-1 1 of 1, haiku-2 1 of 1, sonnet-1 2 of 3 (one fails), sonnet-2 2 of 2.

No rule in this case's list changed since 3e3581d: git diff 3e3581d -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches none of the nine sections, so every verdict follows the 2026-10-22-c grades' standard. The changes are outside the list: the new Formatting bullet under How to use this skill, the reworded "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" (not counted: sonnet-2 lines 128-129 and 139-146 wrap a struct literal inside an {:ok, _} return tuple, which is not a call argument, as the previous sweep did not count sonnet-1's and sonnet-2's; opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 build their structs under a name first), the do: rule's clause-mixing sentence (opus-1's three message/1 block clauses, lines 91-101, hold one expression each but would pass 98 columns on the head's line, so the block is what the rule asks; haiku-2's nullable_string_field/2 block, lines 172-174, likewise; no run wraps a do: body), Before you finish step 1, and testing.md renamed to ex_unit.md with a reworded "Assert with patterns" (no run writes tests).

Closest calls. Match every expected shape: sonnet-2's line 133, defp parse_data(_payment_event_type, data) do, parses every atom other than :refund_created as a payment, so a type added to event_type/1 later is silently parsed as a payment; the 2026-10-21 sweep graded skill-sonnet-2's defp parse_data(_payment_event, data) violated for the same shape, so this is too, and it is Sonnet's only break of the rule. Haiku-2's def parse(_payload), do: {:error, :invalid_payload} (line 99) receives payloads missing an envelope key, with a non-string id or with non-map data; :invalid_payload names no field, so it misnames none, and it goes in checks only, as 2026-10-22-c graded baseline-sonnet-2's and baseline-opus-1's :invalid_payload; its line 157 catch-all also receives a non-string type ("type" => 123 gives {:unsupported_event, 123}, verified), which the previous sweep's skill-haiku-2 put in checks only, so it goes in checks here too.

Multi-clause heads: haiku-2 line 91, def parse(%{"id" => id, "type" => type, "created" => created, "data" => data}) when is_binary(id) and is_map(data) do, binds type and created that no pattern or guard uses (line 99 is the other clause), the shape 2026-10-22-b graded violated in skill-haiku-2 and the baselines' "id, type, created bound in the head". Haiku-1's and haiku-2's parse_event/4 clauses take event_id, created_at and data as whole positional arguments, not destructured fields, and are clean; opus-1's Error.message/1 binds the reason tuple's element next to the tag that selects the clause (lines 91-101), not counted, as before. Struct rule: opus-1's Payments.Webhook.Error (line 81, defexception [:reason]) has @type t (line 88) but no @enforce_keys, the shape the two previous sweeps counted as violated; its other four structs have both.

Comments: sonnet-1's parse/1 doctest expects created_at: ~U[2024-09-22 09:46:40Z] (line 94), but 1727000000 is ~U[2024-09-22 10:13:20Z], so 1 of 3 doctests fails; 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22-b counted the same timestamp as violated under "Include `## Examples` that work as doctests.". Haiku-1's comment above parse_event/4 (lines 102-104) and haiku-2's (lines 101-102) describe the split and then give its reason (a known type with a missing field reports that field instead of falling through), and haiku-2's lines 155-156 give the reason the catch-all returns an error rather than crashing; graded as comments that explain why, as 2026-10-21 graded skill-haiku-1's reason comment, though the first clause of each restates the structure.

Naming: no run has a fetch_* or get_* function (string_field/2, map_field/2, amount_field/2, timestamp_field/2, currency_field/2, required_field/3, field/3, integer_field/2, optional_*_field/2); every variable or parameter named data holds the payload's "data" map. Not counted, as earlier grades did not count similar names: type_name and parsed_data (opus-1), check (haiku-1), valid? (haiku-2), event_data, email and reason (sonnet-1), details (sonnet-2). The with rule: every with in the five files has two to seven steps and no else; a case whose :ok branch calls another fallible function (opus-1 currency_field/2 line 278 and timestamp_field/2 line 263, sonnet-2 timestamp_field/2 line 177) is not counted, as before. Outside the case list: an if inside a case (haiku-1 line 171, haiku-2 line 179) goes under Keep functions short, as before.

Probe of 28 payloads, run in the scratch folder against each compiled file: in all five, an unknown type gives an unsupported-event error, a known type without amount gives {:missing_field, "amount"}, a string amount gives {:invalid_field, "amount"}, refunds without refund_id or payment_id name that field and an out-of-range created gives {:invalid_field, "created"}. Differences: a present nil amount is missing in opus-1 and invalid in the others; a negative amount is accepted only by haiku-2 (is_integer/1 alone); a missing customer_email is accepted by opus-1 and sonnet-1 and rejected by the others; a nil failure_reason on payment.failed is rejected as invalid only by sonnet-1; refunds carry no amount in haiku-1 and haiku-2 and an optional one in sonnet-1; a non-map payload raises in opus-1 (FunctionClauseError) and haiku-1 (BadMapError) and returns an error in the others; haiku-2 returns the unnamed :invalid_payload for a missing or ill-typed id, type, created or data.

Compared with the previous skill sweep (2026-10-22-c at 3e3581d): Match every expected shape moves from Sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-2's parse_data/2 payment catch-all); Comments moves from Sonnet clean to violated (sonnet-1's failing doctest); Naming moves from Haiku violated to clean (no fetch_* in either Haiku run); the multi-clause rule stays Haiku violated (haiku-2, now the parse/1 head) and the struct rule stays Opus violated (an exception without @enforce_keys again). Read required keys, atoms, the with rule and the return-tuple rule stay clean in every tier.
